customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned in a workflow `with:` input, annotated with a `# renovate:` comment on the preceding line (no built-in manager reads action inputs)

packageRules.description: Go toolchain and indirect module updates change the shipped binary like direct ones, so they get the fix type and semantic-release publishes a patch release with them. The :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers preset of config:recommended gives fix to the require depType only, chore (no release) to the rest. Root go.mod only: tools/go.mod feeds make generate and is not linked into the binary.

tflint is installed from a pinned release zip whose sha256 is hardcoded next to the version (security.yml); Renovate can bump the version but not the hash, so its PR always fails the tflint job until TFLINT_SHA256 is updated by hand. Never automerge it (#241 was merged with the job red).

Release tooling runs next to the release credentials: the semantic-release App token, which bypasses the main ruleset, and the GPG key that signs the Registry checksums. Its updates get their own group and are never automerged, whatever the update type, so a maintainer reviews each one. Matched by file, so it covers GoReleaser (custom.regex), the semantic-release packages and their lockfile (npm) and the actions those two workflows use (github-actions); the same action in other workflows keeps its usual automerged group. The commit type is forced to chore: the npm manager gives the semantic-release packages the dependencies depType, which config:recommended would title fix(deps), and a fix title would publish a provider patch release for a tooling bump.

GoReleaser is pinned twice, in goreleaser-release.yml (above) and in goreleaser-check.yml, which validates .goreleaser.yml on every PR. Both pins must move in the same reviewed PR: otherwise the check job runs a newer GoReleaser than the release job for the three days before the ci-tools group automerges, and a config change it accepts can fail at tag time, after the GitHub release and the tag already exist.

gitleaks is installed in gitleaks.yml from a pinned release archive whose sha256 is hardcoded next to the version, like tflint above: Renovate bumps the version but not the hash, so never automerge it. mise.toml pins the same version for the pre-commit hook: both bumps go in one PR, so the hook never runs a newer gitleaks than CI.

Hold anthropic-sdk-go on v1 until #192 is done in major/2.0.0: v2 moves the client to API version 2026-10-21, which is breaking for this provider (temperature, api_keys.workspace_id and the rate-limit group_type are removed, skills come back in their GA shape only, and the API key is sent as Authorization: Bearer instead of x-api-key). v1 minor and patch releases stay allowed. Remove this rule as part of #192, not on its own.

Review every anthropic-sdk-go minor release before it merges, in its own PR: v1 minors have changed what goes over the wire without breaking the build (v1.68.0 stopped sending the skills beta header, v1.75.0 started sending extra input_schema keys, v1.80.0 turned multiagent into a union), and no CI job calls the live API. Its own PR, so the Go dependencies group keeps automerging. Patch releases still automerge with that group.
Never propose a major SDK update, OSV vulnerability-fix PRs included (their allowedVersions replaces any hold above): a new major is the #192 migration, not a dependency bump.

Hold conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits below 9: 10.x needs conventional-changelog-writer@9, but the latest stable @semantic-release/release-notes-generator (14.1.1) pins writer ^8, so generateNotes fails with 'Missing helper'. Lift once release-notes-generator 15 ships with writer 9.

poutine is installed in security.yml from a pinned release archive whose sha256 is hardcoded next to the version, exactly like tflint above: Renovate bumps the version but not the hash, so never automerge it.
